title: Series, bounded operators and the dual
summary: Absolutely summable series as a completeness test; linear operators, boundedness equals continuity; the operator norm and the Banach space B(V,W); the dual space.

objectives.description: Prove that a normed space is Banach if and only if every absolutely summable series is summable, and use the criterion.
Prove that a linear operator between normed spaces is continuous if and only if it is bounded.
Compute or bound operator norms, including for an integral operator, and prove the submultiplicative inequality.
Explain why B(V,W) is a Banach space when W is, and why the dual space is always Banach.

preparation.description: Read lecture 2 notes pages 1–2: summable and absolutely summable series, Proposition 18 and Theorem 19 with its proof.
Read Example 20, Definition 21 and Theorem 22 (continuous iff bounded) with its proof.
Read Definitions 24–25 and Theorems 26–27 (operator norm; B(V,W) is Banach when W is), then Definition 28 (dual space).

activities.title: Lecture 2: series, operators, the dual
activities.instructions: Read the lesson with lecture 2 of the notes. After Theorem 22, close the notes and reprove 'bounded implies continuous' before reading the proof of the converse.

activities.title: Tutorial: operator norms
activities.instructions: Attempt exercises 1 and 2. Exercise 2 is the first operator whose norm you compute exactly; write the inequality and the attaining (or nearly attaining) function separately.

activities.title: Explain: why the summability test is convenient

exitCheck.description: Exercise 2 accepted: the operator norm of the Volterra operator computed as 1 with both the upper bound and the attaining function, and non-surjectivity argued.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Every linear map between normed spaces is continuous, as in finite dimensions.
commonMisconceptions.correction: In infinite dimensions linear maps can be unbounded; differentiation on polynomials with the sup norm is the standard example. Continuity is equivalent to boundedness (Theorem 22), which is a genuine condition.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The operator norm is attained by some unit vector.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The supremum in Definition 25 need not be attained in infinite dimensions; one must argue with a sequence approaching it or show attainment explicitly.
